einzeiler: Answers to listener questions on retirement accounts, active management, and insurance…
kurzfassung: The host answers listener questions covering a wide range of financial topics. Discussions include Roth conversion logistics, ETF availability in 401(k) and 403(b) plans, and the performance data comparing active and passive management. Additional topics address cash equivalent strategies, turning off dividend reinvestment in retirement, and managing variable universal life insurance policies.
stichpunkte: Converting annual spending money into a Roth account before immediate withdrawal provides no tax benefits.
Federal law allows tax-exempt organizations to establish 401(k) plans, which can support ETFs through brokerage windows.
Standard and Poor's scorecard data shows that the vast majority of active managers fail to beat indexes over 15-year periods.
Chasing tiny yield differences in treasuries versus money market accounts often yields minimal financial return relative to the effort.
Disabling dividend and capital gains reinvestment in retirement simplifies portfolio decumulation and cash flow management.
Universal life insurance policies typically feature high costs and inferior investment options compared to standard mutual funds.

clips.hook: No benefit in converting annual spending money
clips.text: Shifting funds meant for yearly expenses into a Roth account right before withdrawal creates no financial advantage because the tax burden remains identical.

clips.hook: 401ks can allow ETFs through brokerage accounts
clips.text: Retirement plan administrators who claim that exchange-traded funds are strictly prohibited in employer plans are incorrect.

clips.hook: 93% of actively managed funds fail to beat the index
clips.text: Long-term performance data reveals that only a tiny fraction of active international fund managers manage to outperform standard market benchmarks.

clips.hook: An extra quarter of a percent is just a nice dinner
clips.text: Chasing fractional yield improvements on large cash balances results in very minor annual dollar gains that barely impact overall wealth.

clips.hook: No point in reinvesting dividends during retirement
clips.text: Retirees in the withdrawal phase benefit from routing dividends and capital gains directly into cash accounts to fund expenses and aid rebalancing.

beschreibung:
Should retirement spending pass through a Roth? Can a nonprofit offer a 401(k) with ETFs? Does active management really win overseas? Don works through a packed listener-question episode covering Roth conversions, retirement-plan rollovers, SPIVA versus Morningstar, Treasuries and CDs, dividend reinvestment in retirement, and whether a variable universal life policy still earns its keep.
